annotation.reasoning_summary: Polygons represent housing-block/property footprints of housing association ownership, so the mapped thing is discrete objects rather than a tessellation or patch; numeric fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point geometry and the layer maps individual archaeological find sites/cesspit locations with addresses and photos; the mapped feature is the object/site, not an amount or event.
Point geometry with 92 archaeological find locations; each point represents a distinct mapped archaeological object/location, not a measurement or event.
Polygon features mark selected archaeological sites/vindplaatsen with names, addresses, and reports; they are discrete mapped objects, not a full tessellation or a general patch/coverage layer.
Polygons mark BBQ restriction/permission areas in parks, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded applicability zones.

Polygon areas for protected conservation/conservation-status zones; they are selected bounded cultural-historical areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded applicability/protection areas.
Point features mark survey/inventory occurrences of wild bees at locations, with year as observation time; this fits EventDS rather than object or amount.
Point locations show the main phenomenon as a numeric amount of honey-bee hives/colonies per location ('aantal kasten/volken'), so this is PointDS with AmountDS.

The layer is a zone-based soil quality map with polygons that partition the area into zones, so it fits VectorTessellation. The zones represent areas where soil quality conditions apply rather than discrete objects, so PatchDS.
Point features represent individual trees (a discrete mapped object), not measurements or events. Numeric fields are attributes of each tree, so ObjectDS, with point geometry.
Point geometry with 70k records; each point represents an individual tree object, not a measurement or event. Numeric fields are attributes of trees, so ObjectDS.
Point geometry with individual tree records; the mapped phenomenon is identifiable real-world objects (trees), not measurements or events.
Point features represent individual trees, which are distinct real-world objects; numeric fields are just attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point layer of distinct compost initiatives at specific street/address locations; the mapped thing is each initiative/object, not a measurement or event.
Polygon areas named as camera/overlastgebieden indicate selected affected zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; classify by the patch/area-of-applicability rule.
Point features map individual trees as identifiable objects; numeric/text fields are attributes and the layer is not about measurements or events.
Point geometry and the map describes discrete sensors/telsystemen as the mapped objects; the numeric fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Polygons are selected cultural-historical areas and protected zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the layer maps where cultural-historical value applies, so PatchDS.
Point layer of reported knotweed occurrences; each point represents a mapped infestation/object-like observation rather than a measurement, event, or area zone.
Point features mark ecological bottlenecks/passages to be resolved, with status and realisation year indicating planned/realized occurrences rather than point objects or measurements.

Polygons represent selected potential wind-energy areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded phenomenon/application zones; numeric MW/output fields are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.

Point layer of election voting locations/stemlocaties with circle sizes encoding vote totals and percentages; the main mapped phenomenon is numeric amount at points, not just the facilities themselves.
Point features mark reported oak processionary caterpillar nests/removed nests at locations, with real-time mutations over time; the decisive rules are point geometry and event/change over time.
Polygon areas represent pedicab restriction/permission zones, not a full tessellation or discrete objects; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded applicability/restriction areas.
Point features representing pedicab stand locations/pitches; the mapped thing is a distinct object/place, not a measurement or event.
Point geometry with address/BA G verblijfsobject records; the layer maps identifiable non-residential objects/facilities by function, not a measurement or event.

Polygon layer classifies block-street areas by dominant function mix (Wonen/Voorzieningen/Werken), a full-area thematic classification over tessellated regions, so Geometry is VectorTessellation and Entity is CoverageDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete administrative/reporting-unit partition, so geometry is VectorTessellation and entity is LatticeDS.
Neighborhood/buurt polygons form a reporting-unit partition of Amsterdam; the decisive rule is reporting units -> LatticeDS, with polygon regions covering the area as a tessellation.
Neighborhood polygons form a reporting-unit tessellation (buurten/wijken/stadsdelen), so the geometry is VectorTessellation and the entity is LatticeDS rather than ObjectDS or PatchDS.
Administrative/reporting-unit neighborhoods (buurten/wijken/stadsdelen) that partition the study area, so VectorTessellation and LatticeDS.
City districts are administrative/reporting units that partition Amsterdam, so the polygons form a tessellation and the main entity is LatticeDS.
Administrative reporting units (stadsdelen/boroughs) that partition the city area, so geometry is a tessellation and entity is a reporting-unit lattice.

The layer depicts Amsterdam neighbourhoods/district areas (buurten, wijken, stadsdelen, gebieden), which are reporting/statistical units forming a partition, so it is a VectorTessellation with LatticeDS.

The layer maps Amsterdam neighbourhoods/district areas ('buurten, wijken, gebieden, stadsdelen'), which are reporting/admin units forming a near-complete area partition, so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS.
The layer shows neighbourhoods/districts/areas in Amsterdam that function as reporting/administrative units, so the polygons form a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS.
The layer shows Amsterdam neighbourhood/area units (buurten, wijken, gebieden, stadsdelen) as polygons that function as reporting/statistical units, so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS is the best fit.

Polygon areas show industrial noise contour zones, which are selected phenomenon areas rather than reporting units or objects; this fits PatchDS. Geometry is PlainVectorRegion because the polygons do not form a full tessellation of Amsterdam.
Polygon isolines/classes for aircraft noise levels (55–70+ dB); this is a contour/value-band map, not a tessellation or object layer.
Polygon contours/bands of calculated noise levels (50-55, 55-60, etc.); the decisive rule is contour/interval-zone representation rather than objects or reporting units.

Polygon contour polygons for traffic noise; the layer maps noise level bands (Lden/Lnight, dB classes) rather than objects or reporting units, so ContourDS. The polygons are discrete contour zones, not a full tessellation.

Point features represent voting locations/stembureaus, i.e. identifiable real-world places/facilities. The numeric vote fields are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon, so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point geometry with one feature per roof/location; metadata describes a catalogue of green/multifunctional roofs, so the mapped thing is a discrete object rather than an amount or event.
Land use 2017 is an area-wide thematic classification over polygon units, so the polygons form a tessellated coverage rather than discrete objects or patches.
Point geometry with 200 named historical building/archeology locations; each point represents a distinct object/place, not a measurement or event.

The layer shows three polygonal boundary shapes used to represent Amsterdam-related areas for area comparison, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The mapped features are the bounded places themselves (municipality, agglomeration, metropolitan region), so ObjectDS fits best.
Polygon areas are selected dog run/ban/restriction zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded applicability/restriction areas.

Polygon areas represent the Amsterdam Main Green Structure as selected zones where green functions and policy constraints apply; not a full tessellation or reporting units. PatchDS fits the bounded applicability areas described in the map text.
Point geometry with 1462 individual elm tree locations; the layer maps distinct trees/objects, not measurements or events.
Point features represent individual youth/student housing projects or buildings; the decisive rule is ObjectDS for distinct real-world facilities, not AmountDS despite the housing counts.
Point geometries map individual chestnut trees as identifiable objects; the layer is a tree inventory with species and infestation status, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features with numeric values (Maaiveld, GLG) represent sampled measurements in the climate drought layer; the decisive rule is PointMeasuresDS for point-based measurements.
Region polygons map flood-risk/overstroming zones with chance and depth classes; this is a selected phenomenon area (PatchDS), not a reporting unit or full tessellation.

Point geometries mark distinct market locations; the layer is about fixed markets as named real-world places, so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS/PatchDS. Market times and categories are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point geometry with named green monuments/big trees as discrete mapped features; the layer is about identifiable objects, not measurements, network, or area tessellation.
Point features represent individual monumental trees, a discrete mapped object rather than measurements or zones.
Point geometries represent individual monuments/preserved buildings or sites; the layer is about identifiable monuments, not measurements or events.
Point locations mark actual plant occurrences at sites; the key layer meaning is presence of protected wall flora at those locations rather than a continuous measurement or network.
Point layer of NO2 monitoring locations; the main phenomenon is measured air-quality values sampled at points, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.
Point layer of NO2 measurement locations; each feature is a sampling station/buoy point measuring a continuous air-quality phenomenon, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.

Polygons represent the Oergeul as a bounded phenomenon/affected zone around the IJ, not a reporting unit or full tessellation; the decisive rule is PatchDS for a selected geologic area where conditions apply.
Point layer of boreholes/soundings with measured subsoil values; the main phenomenon is sampled measurements at point locations, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.
The layer maps named development neighbourhoods (buurten) in Amsterdam, which are reporting/administrative units and form a near-partition of the study area, so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS.
Point features represent individual public toilet facilities and related installations; the layer maps distinct objects, not measurements or events.

Polygon layer of 101 buurten/stadsdelen used as reporting units for overnight policy conditions; this fits a near-complete territorial partition (VectorTessellation) and reporting-unit aggregation (LatticeDS).
Polygon areas are discrete zones for parking standards; the map describes area-based rules for new development, so the decisive rule is PatchDS (applicability area), not ObjectDS.
Polygons map named parks/green spaces as discrete managed places, not a tessellation or reporting unit. ObjectDS fits the mapped feature; the area field is just an attribute.

Polygon postcode areas form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so geometry is a tessellation. The decisive entity rule is reporting/statistical unit: postcode4 areas used to aggregate addresses, which fits LatticeDS rather than ObjectDS or PatchDS.
Polygon postcode4 areas form a reporting-unit tessellation; the decisive rule is reporting/statistical units (postcode/buurt) -> LatticeDS.
Postcode6 polygons are reporting units derived from addresses, and the layer forms a tessellation of postcode areas; reporting-unit rule takes precedence over object/patch hints.
LineString features represent Amsterdam transport infrastructure networks (plus and main networks); network system is the decisive entity rule.

Polygons mark Amsterdam pedestrian plus/net priority zones from a traffic policy map, so the main meaning is a bounded applicability area rather than a full tessellation or discrete object; classify as patch.
Point geometry with named locations/camera or sensor sites; the map marks distinct privacy-related objects/locations, not amounts, events, or areas.

Point geometry with each point marking a privacy-related study/analysis occurrence in public space; the layer is about where these investigations/monitoring activities happen, so EventDS is the best fit.
Point layer of camera/sensor locations; the map mainly shows where privacy-relevant data processing exists at specific places, so ExistenceDS fits better than AmountDS or ObjectDS.

Point features are voting locations, but the layer mainly maps numeric election totals/percentages shown by circle size and pie charts, so this is a point-based AmountDS rather than an object or event layer.
Polygon patches showing where drainage/high-groundwater rainproof issues or measures apply; not a full tessellation or reporting units, so PlainVectorRegion + PatchDS.
Polygons are hydro units tied to buurten/wijken and model reporting areas, so this is a near-partition of the study area and a reporting-unit lattice rather than objects or patches.

Polygon areas mark rainproof bottleneck zones where water-overload applies; this is a selected phenomenon patch rather than a full tessellation or discrete object. The reporting-unit terms are present, but the layer is about vulnerable areas/locations for overlast, not administrative statistics.

Polygons mark model-derived water-overlast/problem areas from the Rainproof simulation, not a reporting-unit tessellation or discrete objects; this fits PatchDS, with PlainVectorRegion since the polygons do not form a complete partition.
Point geometry with each feature representing a distinct religious facility/building at an address; object-based place mapping, not amounts or events.

The layer maps sidewalk segments as LineString features; the main phenomenon is sidewalk width/comfort level and obstacle space-claim amounts along those line segments, so LineDS with AmountDS fits the amount-on-linear-features rule.
Line geometries represent a route/infrastructure system under a traffic regulation decision; the decisive rule is NetworkDS for connected road/transport lines, not AmountDS or ObjectDS.
Point geometries map distinct public sport facilities/playgrounds; the layer is about identifiable objects/places, not measurements or events.
Point locations of city farming sites/locations; each point represents a distinct real-world place or facility, so PointDS + ObjectDS.

Polygons are discrete sites/parks for city farming, not a full tessellation. The decisive entity rule is ObjectDS because each polygon maps a named agricultural location/facility, with strong object keywords and no patch/coverage/reporting-unit meaning.
Point features mark where space-seeker placements/establishments happened over the past 9 years; the decisive rule is event/occurrence at point locations.
The layer is titled Major streets / Stadsstraten and contains LineString features, so it represents a street/route network rather than individual objects or amounts.
Line geometries and the layer describes district heating/cooling transport lines; this is a connected utility network, so NetworkDS.

Polygon buffers are used to depict district heating/cooling network areas, and the metadata explicitly says transport lines are simplified and wijk lines buffered to polygons. Main phenomenon is a utility network, so NetworkDS; polygons are not a full tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion.

Polygons represent discrete housing development projects/strategic sites with project names and planned dwelling totals; this is object-like rather than a reporting-unit tessellation or patch zone. The numeric fields are attributes of projects, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point features represent named local food and urban farming locations/facilities with addresses and categories; this is a point object layer, not a measure or event layer.
LineString features plus metadata describe the tram/metro network of stations, stops, and lines; this is a connected transport network, not a numeric amount or object layer.
LineString features represent the tram/metro line network; the map description explicitly says it visualizes stations, stops, and lines, so NetworkDS is the decisive entity.
Point geometries representing tram stops and metro stations, but the layer’s main phenomenon is the transit network of stops and lines; network rule takes precedence.
Point geometries represent tram stops and metro stations, and the layer is explicitly a station/stop network rather than isolated objects; network is the decisive entity rule.

Point features represent individual traffic-light-controlled intersections (distinct mapped objects). Numeric years/status are attributes, not the main phenomenon; the layer is not a measurement or network dataset.
Line features represent road links, and the main mapped phenomenon is traffic intensity/prognosis values on those links (etmaal and period volumes), so LineDS + AmountDS.
Point features are voting locations/stemlocaties, and the main mapped phenomenon is numeric election results and turnout amounts at those locations, so PointDS + AmountDS.
Point layer of individual trees; each point represents a distinct real-world object (a tree), not a measurement or event.
Point layer of distinct traffic information system objects; metadata says each click shows more info about that object, so this is ObjectDS rather than an amount or event.
Point features represent distinct traffic information system objects/facilities; map description says each clickable object is an installation, so this is PointDS with ObjectDS.
Point features mark breeding/nesting locations of birds at specific addresses/structures; this is a mapped set of identifiable objects/places, not a measurement or event layer.
Point geometry and the layer maps individual Vondelpark benches as identifiable managed objects; the adoption status is just an attribute, not the main phenomenon.

Line geometry with street-segment features; the main mapped phenomenon is walkability/width and crowding-derived scores along each street section, so AmountDS is the best fit rather than object or network.
Point geometry with 226 features; the layer maps distinct wall art works as identifiable objects at locations, not measurements or events.
Polygons represent welstand zones/areas with policy levels, not reporting units or full coverage; this fits a tessellation of bounded applicability areas, so PatchDS.

Polygon layer of Amsterdam welstand systems forms a citywide thematic partition of areas with different design-policy levels, so Geometry is VectorTessellation. The polygons mainly mark policy/condition zones rather than discrete objects, so Entity is PatchDS.
Point features mark WWII attack/incidents with dates; the main phenomenon is where and when events occurred, so PointDS + EventDS.
Polygons map housing plan sites, but the main phenomenon is the numeric plan supply (Totaal and dwelling counts); this is an amount layer, not reporting units or full tessellation.
Point layer of self-build plot projects; each point represents a distinct project/site (object), not a measurement or event.

Polygon layer of individual roof/pand areas partitioning the city; the map is an indicative applicability/placement-opportunity zone for solar panels on heritage-related buildings, so PatchDS rather than ObjectDS. The many polygons form a near-complete area coverage over Amsterdam, supporting VectorTessellation.

Point geometries map solar panel systems with numeric main attributes (detected panels and estimated watt-peak); the layer is about quantities of detected solar installations rather than point objects only.
Point features mark named swimming water locations and facilities (official swim/spel sites); this is a set of distinct places/objects, not measurements or events.
